summary: The ML platform landscape in 2026 has matured into a $4.39B market dominated by cloud-native suites that cover the full lifecycle from experiment tracking through production monitoring, with Azure ML, AWS SageMaker, and Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform leading enterprise readiness benchmarks. Platforms like Databricks Mosaic AI have expanded beyond data engineering into unified data-plus-AI governance, while specialized tools like Weights & Biases and DataRobot fill niche gaps in experiment tracking and no-code AutoML respectively. You need a dedicated ML platform when you require reproducible pipelines, model versioning, governance, and scalable training infrastructure at scale; if you simply need inference from a pre-built model, a model API endpoint is sufficient.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go for compute, storage, and managed endpoints; free tier for workspace; enterprise agreements available
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-heavy enterprises requiring mature MLOps, governance, and deep Azure ecosystem integration

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker
capabilities: Managed training jobs and distributed training
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use for compute instances, storage, and inference; Studio has no additional charge; costs scale quickly with usage
platforms.best_for: AWS-native organizations needing breadth of ML infrastructure control and tight integration with S3, Glue, and other AWS services

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
capabilities: MLflow 3.x experiment tracking and model registry
Feature engineering on Delta Lake / Unity Catalog
Governance and lineage via Unity Catalog
platforms.pricing: DBU (Databricks Unit) consumption-based pricing; varies by cloud provider and workload type; enterprise licensing available
platforms.best_for: Data-centric organizations that want unified data engineering, analytics, and AI governance on a lakehouse architecture across multiple clouds

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
capabilities: Managed model training and hyperparameter tuning
AutoML for vision, text, tabular, and video
Model Garden (access to Gemini, third-party, and open models)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute hour, prediction request, and managed feature; custom enterprise agreements available
platforms.best_for: GCP-native teams and organizations with data-heavy or generative AI use cases, especially those building on Gemini model family

platforms.name: Dataiku
capabilities: Visual and code-based ML pipeline builder
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription licensing; pricing not publicly listed; free Community Edition available for individuals
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting a collaborative, low-code-to-pro-code platform that bridges data science teams and business stakeholders

platforms.name: DataRobot
capabilities: Model training across dozens of algorithms
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; consumption-based add-ons; pricing not publicly listed
platforms.best_for: Enterprises prioritizing automated model building, explainability, and regulated-industry compliance with minimal ML engineering overhead

platforms.name: Domino Data Lab
platforms.cloud: Multi-cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) and on-premises / hybrid
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; pricing not publicly listed; based on compute usage and seat licensing
platforms.best_for: Large regulated enterprises (pharma, finance) needing strong reproducibility, governance, and hybrid/on-prem deployment flexibility

platforms.name: H2O.ai
capabilities: H2O AutoML for automated model training
Driverless AI for automated feature engineering
H2O LLM Studio for LLM fine-tuning
platforms.pricing: Open-source H2O-3 is free; Driverless AI and enterprise products are subscription-based; pricing not publicly listed
platforms.best_for: Organizations needing powerful AutoML, interpretability, and LLM fine-tuning with options to run fully on-premises

platforms.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
capabilities: Integration with major training frameworks (PyTorch, TF, JAX, HuggingFace)
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals; Team plan starts at $50/user/month; Enterprise pricing available; self-hosted option
platforms.best_for: ML research teams and production ML engineers who need best-in-class experiment tracking, reproducibility, and model lineage without a full platform switch

platforms.name: MLflow
platforms.cloud: Self-hosted (any cloud or on-premises); managed via Databricks
capabilities: Plugin ecosystem for AutoML and deployment targets
Integration with virtually all ML frameworks
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; managed version included in Databricks subscription
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting open-source, framework-agnostic experiment tracking and model registry that integrates with any existing infrastructure

platforms.name: Modal
capabilities: Serverless GPU compute for training and fine-tuning
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second compute; GPU instances from ~$0.74/hr (A10G) to $4.53/hr (H100); generous free tier ($30/month credits)
platforms.best_for: ML engineers and startups wanting serverless, code-first GPU infrastructure for training and deployment without managing Kubernetes or cloud ML consoles

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.cloud: Any Kubernetes cluster (self-hosted, AWS, Azure, GCP, on-prem)
capabilities: Kubeflow Pipelines for ML workflow orchestration
Training Operator for distributed training (PyTorch, TF, MPI)
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free; infrastructure costs only; managed distributions available from cloud providers
platforms.best_for: DevOps-mature teams and platform engineers who want full Kubernetes-native ML infrastructure control without vendor lock-in
